reason: B gives three clean nested levels (aldehyde/ethanol detoxification core, xenobiotic biotransformation, xenobiotic metabolism plus transport and drug ADME), whereas A repeats the same xenobiotic context across 11 overlapping themes and adds off-target ones such as tryptophan/kynurenine and bile-acid homeostasis.

Both cover RAS GAP/RASopathy mutants, ERK negative feedback, oncogenic RAF/BRAF and the broad RTK level, but B spreads these across 34 heavily overlapping MAPK-feedback themes, and its only additions (FGFR/oncogenic fusion and an odd IL-6 grouping) don't justify the clutter.

A covers the TLS core, polymerase switching/replication, NER and BER gap filling, UV repair, somatic hypermutation and a broad genome-maintenance level in 12 themes; B repeats these in many near-duplicate intermediate combinations, and its only real addition is a mismatch-repair and DSB/fork-processing level.

Both reflect the same facets (EDA/EDAR ectodermal appendage development, keratinocyte/skin, B-cell CD27/ICOS costimulation), but B splits the ectodermal context into about ten near-identical tooth/hair/skin variants; its one useful addition is a broader T-cell CD28 costimulation theme.

A gives a concise tryptophan-kynurenine-to-NAD+ core with nicotinate/NAD salvage and redox levels; B duplicates these with mitochondrial/amino-acid variants and adds weakly related methylglyoxal, CoA/PDH and xenobiotic-metabolism themes.

Both wrongly group N-terminal acetylation with lysine/histone acetylation, chromatin remodelling, tubulin modification and circadian/metabolic contexts, but A does so in 14 themes while B repeats them in 25 near-duplicates; B's one apt addition is a co-translational N-terminal lipidation theme.
